name: Notburga-Museum Eben am Achensee
kurzbeschreibung: The Notburga Museum in Eben am Achensee: the only museum honoring Tyrol's most beloved folk saint, Notburga of Rattenberg, in the baroque rectory from 2004.
beschreibung:
Overview

The traditional Notburga Museum is located in the idyllic pilgrimage village of Eben am Achensee at the entrance to the Achensee valley in the Tyrolean district of Schwaz. Housed in the listed rooms of the historic rectory directly next to the magnificent baroque pilgrimage church of St. Notburga, the house is the only museum in Austria dedicated exclusively to the most famous and beloved female folk saint of the Alpine region: Saint Notburga of Rattenberg (approx. 1265–1313). Opened in 2004 and awarded the renowned Tyrolean Museum Prize, this specialized museum offers profound insights into medieval piety, Tyrolean social history, and the vibrant popular beliefs of past centuries.

Route & Requirements

Notburga lived in the 13th century as a simple maid at Rottenburg Castle in Buch near Jenbach and later on a farm in Eben. Throughout her life, she selflessly championed the poor, the sick, and the maids. The legend of the Sickle Miracle became world-famous: when her master wanted to force her to continue harvesting on the eve of Sunday, Notburga threw her sickle into the sky, where it remained suspended in the air as confirmation of divine rest on a holiday.

Visit & Arrival

The Notburga Museum is open from early May to late October: Tuesdays to Sundays from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM (closed on Mondays). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €6.00, seniors and groups approx. €5.00, children and teenagers up to 18 years have free admission! With the regional Achensee Erlebniscard, the visit is free. The adjacent pilgrimage church can be visited daily for free. Arrival by public transport: ÖBB to Jenbach station, from there take the traditional Achenseebahn (steam cog railway) or bus line 4080 directly to the Maurach/Eben Kirche stop (approx. two minutes walk). By car: Inntal motorway A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee), on the Achenseestraße B181 about five kilometers up to Eben; free parking is available directly at the rectory.

Tips

Access to the museum on the ground floor and the forecourt to the pilgrimage church are barrier-free; assistance is available for the upper exhibition rooms in the historic rectory. Be sure to allow enough time to also visit the church nave with its magnificent Rococo ceiling frescoes. The traditional Notburgatag on September 13th attracts thousands of visitors annually with a splendid traditional costume procession. It is recommended to combine your museum visit with a stroll along Lake Achensee to enjoy the picturesque landscape.
